newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian PM says political crisis worsening.
newsitem.headline: Albanian PM says political crisis worsening.

text.p: Marathon talks between Prime Minister Bashkim Fino and political parties have not only failed to produce agreement on ground rules for planned elections but worsened Albania's crisis, his office said on Tuesday.
All-day meetings with parties of his national unity government on Tuesday did not yield a compromises on procedures for the elections, which most parties are now threatening to boycott.

The vote, targeted for the end of June, would a key step against a resurgence of the anarchic violence that swept Albania in February and March. Rebellion erupted after many thousands of people lost life savings in collapsed pyramid investment schemes.

"Although the debate continued all Monday it failed not only to bring compromise or come near to compromise but on the contrary took Albania to the edge of a deeper crisis with unforeseen consequences," Fino's office said in a statement.

A spokesman for Fino said the prime minister would again consult various parties but also the international community, which has repeatedly warned of a withdrawal of foreign aid barring an election agreement.

Paramilitary violence has subsided markedly in recent weeks and a Western-led multinational force is now safeguarding aid shipments in Albania. But some regions remain lawless. Nine people were reported killed in gunfire since Sunday.
Rumours abounded that European envoy Franz Vranitzky would be called on to make another troubleshooting mission to Albania, although five previous trips have failed to hammer out an accord.
The parties threatening to boycott the vote say current election laws favour rightist President Sali Berisha and his former ruling Democratic Party.

Genc Pollo, a senior Democratic Party official, said there was still disagreement over how many seats should be decided by proportional representation and how many by first-past-the-post majority voting.
"This takes us back to where we were four weeks ago," Pollo said.

The Democratic Party and its main rival, the Socialists, have been clashing for months over electoral rules. The Democrats favour more majority voting while the Socialists back more proportional representation.
